name: Female Steeder
publication: Out of the Abyss - D&D Encounters
sourceRole: The local original adventure is the rules and encounter source. The public link identifies the publisher’s edition or errata.
sourceDistinctions: The Encounters block explicitly gives a 90-ft. maximum and a 30-ft. minimum speed for Leap. The Maerimydra block has its own wording.
appearanceEvidence: The Encounters edition describes female steeders as large Underdark tarantulas trained as mounts. The portrait depicts that form.
habitatEvidence: Appendix C p. 62 describes Underdark steeders trained by duergar.

name: Male Steeder
publication: Out of the Abyss - D&D Encounters
sourceRole: The local original adventure is the rules and encounter source. The public link identifies the publisher’s edition or errata.
sourceDistinctions: The actions continue on p. 63. The printed Bite line gives average 7 and roll 1d8 + 2. Both printed figures are preserved.
appearanceEvidence: Appendix C p. 62 describes males as Underdark tarantulas as big as ponies.
habitatEvidence: Appendix C p. 62 describes Underdark steeders trained by duergar.

name: Female Steeder
sourceRole: The local original adventure is the rules and encounter source. The public link identifies the publisher’s edition or errata.
sourceDistinctions: Page 54 gives a 120-ft. Leap and gives no minimum speed.
appearanceEvidence: The Encounters edition describes female steeders as large Underdark tarantulas trained as mounts. The portrait depicts that form.
habitatEvidence: The adventure places female steeders at the Maerimydra assault and provides two available mounts on p. 28.

name: Spider King
sourceRole: The local original adventure is the rules and encounter source. The public link identifies the publisher’s edition or errata.
sourceDistinctions: The adventure sets fixed HP to 44 and changes Perception, passive Perception and two saves. It adds the two-head advantages and protection from surprise by intruders in its domain. The base giant spider block has 26 (4d10 + 4) HP. The publisher adventure errata list no change to the Spider King.
appearanceEvidence: Page 74 explicitly describes the two heads and vaguely humanoid shape. Chitin and coloration are editorial portrait details.
habitatEvidence: The Dire Den encounter is in the Whorlstone Tunnels on p. 74.

name: Young Bulette
section: Chapter 5: Temple of the Elder Elemental Eye
sourceRole: The local original adventure is the rules and encounter source. The public link identifies the publisher’s edition or errata.
sourceDistinctions: The publisher adventure errata list no change to the Bulette Kennels.

Area G13 calls for the Rhinoceros statistics with Bite in place of Gore. The Beast type comes from that proxy. The adventure supplies no separate damage type, so Bite retains the proxy’s bludgeoning damage.
appearanceEvidence: Area G13 identifies the juvenile bulettes. Armored anatomy is an editorial depiction of the juvenile from its reused portrait.
habitatEvidence: The three young bulettes are in the northern pens of area G13 on p. 139.

name: Golden Stag
sourceRole: The local original adventure is the rules and encounter source. The public link identifies the publisher’s edition or errata.
sourceDistinctions: The local adventure text already uses The Golden Stag as the heading. The road-event table retains The Golden Hind.

The p. 35 encounter directs the DM to use Elk statistics. The publisher errata changes the older table label The Golden Hind to The Golden Stag. The Elk supplement gives no separate damage type for the additional Charge dice.
